title: Seoul Real Estate 2026: Prices, Trends & Investment Guide
description: Seoul real estate market 2026 — which neighborhoods are rising, where to invest, and what foreigners need to know about buying property in Korea.
content:
Seoul's real estate market has experienced dramatic swings in recent years, but 2026 shows signs of stabilization following the government's sustained intervention policies. Here's what buyers, investors, and curious renters need to know.

Market Overview 2026

After the peak market of 2021 and subsequent corrections, Seoul apartment prices have found a new equilibrium approximately 15-20% below 2021 highs. The government's expanded jeonse (전세, long-term rental deposit) protections have improved the rental market for tenants.

Neighborhood Price Guide

Gangnam-gu (강남구)

Still Seoul's most expensive district. Premium apartments in areas like Daechi-dong and Apgujeong range from ₩2-5 billion for 85㎡ units. International schools, premium amenities, and the Han River premium drive pricing.

Mapo-gu (마포구)

Yeonnam-dong and Sangam-dong have seen the strongest appreciation in 2026. Creative industry workers and digital nomads drive demand. Relatively affordable entry points with strong rental yields.

Seongdong-gu (성동구)

Seongsu-dong's cultural revival has driven residential prices up 40% over 3 years. Now pricing out original residents — a pattern Seoul has seen before in Hongdae and Garosu-gil.

💡 Foreigner Note: Foreign nationals can purchase property in South Korea without restrictions, but must register the purchase with the Bank of Korea within 60 days. Consult a Korean real estate attorney before proceeding.

Investment Outlook

Most analysts expect modest appreciation (3-7%) in 2026-2027 in the Mapo-Seongdong corridor. The GTX (Great Train Express) lines under construction will significantly impact property values along the route when they open 2027-2029.
